title: Ruby Exercises
description: Read each example in its lesson first. Predict the result, then check your answer. The notes explain the idea and one common mistake.

exercises.question: puts prints a value and moves to a new line. Quoted letters make a string. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: puts writes the string and supplies a newline. Quote marks are not printed. Keep matching quotes around text.

exercises.question: Ruby variables give names to values. The plus sign adds numbers. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: pencils holds 3. The expression adds 2 and passes 5 to puts. Do not put number values in quotes when you want maths.

exercises.question: Inside double quotes, #{name} places a value into text. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Ruby replaces #{name} with Ravi in the double-quoted string. Single-quoted strings do not expand #{name}.

exercises.code:
score = 8
if score >= 5
  puts "Pass"
else
  puts "Try again"
end
exercises.question: if runs a block when its rule is true. Ruby closes this block with end. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The score passes the test. Only the first puts runs. Remember the final end for the if block.

exercises.question: An array keeps values in order. The first index is zero. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The array positions are 0 and 1. The second position contains dog. An index past the list gives nil, not a new item.

exercises.question: each visits each item. The name between vertical bars is the current item. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The block input n takes each number in turn. puts runs once per value. Use the current item n inside the block.

exercises.code:
def twice(n)
  n * 2
end
puts twice(4)
exercises.question: A method is a named set of steps. Ruby returns the last expression by default. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The method receives 4 as n. Its final expression gives 8. Keep the calculation as the last expression if it is the answer.

exercises.code:
book = { title: "Moon Trip", pages: 24 }
puts book[:title]
exercises.question: A hash pairs keys with values. :title is a symbol used as a key. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The :title symbol selects Moon Trip. :pages would select a different value. The symbol :title and the string "title" are different keys.

exercises.question: map makes a new array from the result of a block for each item. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: map collects 4 and 6 from its block. join inserts the comma and space. map returns a new array; it does not replace the old one.

exercises.question: nil means no value. The || operator chooses the right side when the left side is nil or false. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The left value is nil, so the fallback Guest is selected. Zero and empty strings count as true in Ruby.

exercises.question: A class groups data and methods. initialize runs when a new object is made. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: initialize stores blue in @colour. The label method reads that object field. @colour belongs to the object; colour is only a local input.

exercises.code:
begin
  puts Integer("cat")
rescue ArgumentError
  puts "Use a whole number"
end
exercises.question: rescue handles an error of a named kind. Integer tries to read a whole number from text. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Integer cannot read cat as a whole number. rescue catches the ArgumentError. Handle the error you expect instead of hiding every error.
